property_summary: After depositing an amount X from this contract into c, c.balances[this] is greater-than-or-equal to X (deposit does not decrease the depositor's recorded balance).
Calling Deposit with any nonzero wei value sent should not revert (i.e., Deposit succeeds for any positive payment).
When calling Deposit with a positive ether value, the call must not revert (Deposit always succeeds for any caller sending >0 wei).

For any caller and positive deposit value, calling Deposit with that value does not revert when the caller's prior recorded balance is at most address(c).balance (i.e., deposit cannot underflow the stored balance for callers with small on-chain recorded balance relative to contract balance).

property_summary: For every caller and deposit amount, Deposit increases that caller's balances entry by the deposited msg.value; the mutant that subtracts msg.value can cause Collect to produce a balances entry that is lower in the mutant than in the reference for some fuzzed inputs (i.e., balances[key] after Collect is always >=0 and only increases via Deposit in the reference, but the mutant can make balances decrease on Deposit causing balances to differ after Collect).

For any actor and amounts, calling Deposit then Collect should never make some other address's stored balance increase in the reference; the mutant (which decrements on Deposit) can cause balances to differ after Collect for some inputs — we assert that after a Deposit+Collect roundtrip by an actor, no non-depositor address has a larger balance than before (reference preserves non-depositors' balances, mutant can violate).

Invariant: For any caller and any deposit amount, the sum of all stored balances in C never decreases after a Deposit call (total stored balances is non-decreasing); the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can reduce the total stored balances, so after a sequence Deposit then Collect the total stored balances can be smaller in the mutant than in the reference.

After funding an account via Deposit (or receive) and then calling Collect for some amount, the reference contract always leaves the caller's balances[msg.sender] equal to its previous balance minus the collected amount (i.e., Collect only decreases the caller's own balance by the collected amount when allowed); the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make balances[msg.sender] differ (not follow that equality) for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor, after they Deposit some value and then call Collect(x) (when Collect executes without revert), the reference contract's balances for every address never decreases as a result of Deposit (i.e., balances[key]_after >= balances[key]_before for all keys), but the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make some address's stored balance decrease, so there exist fuzzed inputs where balances differ after Collect.
After calling Deposit(x) from an address, that address's recorded balance is at least x (i.e., balances[msg.sender] >= deposited amount).
